content: Project identity, stated by Xenofon on 2026-08-04: 'shared-memory-monitor' is a SISTER PROJECT of the Shared Memory framework and MUST STAY DISTINCT. It is not a spelling variant, not a section of the framework, and must never be merged into 'shared-memory-GitHub' by an alias map or a normalisation pass. This matters because it is actively at risk: the entity-vote backfill that infers a parked fact's project from the projects of facts sharing its entities was validated by holding out 390 facts with known projects, and EVERY error it made was a sister project absorbed into the larger one — three of six were shared-memory-monitor facts read as shared-memory-GitHub, one of them at 95 percent agreement across 20 supporting facts. A sister project shares most of its vocabulary with the project beside it, so a confident vote is exactly what a misfiled sister-project fact looks like, and raising the agreement threshold does not fix it. Only unanimity measured safe (100 percent accurate on 57 holdout facts), which is why the vote writes automatically only when unanimous and otherwise proposes to the operator with the competing projects shown. Contrast with 'Shared Memory Framework', 'Shared_Memory' and 'shared-memory', which ARE the same project as shared-memory-GitHub and were merged on the same day.

Shared Memory Monitor dashboard UX lessons (project: shared-memory-monitor, domain: ui-ux):

PROBLEMS DIAGNOSED: (1) Triple sticky chrome (header + alert + 7-chip KPI strip) consumes ~40% laptop viewport before content. (2) max-width 1280px wastes horizontal space on wide monitors. (3) Same metrics repeated 3–4× (KPI strip, hero, primary row, pipeline queues) — increases scroll, trains users to skip (Gestalt redundancy). (4) Operational data (throughput, cumulative cleared, raw samples table) buried in collapsed <details> — violates progressive disclosure: hide complexity, not operator data. (5) Chart.js canvases inside collapsed details may render at zero width on first paint.

UX PRINCIPLES TO APPLY: Shneiderman mantra — overview first, zoom/filter, details on demand (schema breakdown = on demand; trends/samples = overview). Nielsen progressive disclosure. F-pattern scanning — one canonical home per metric. Fitts law — range selector stays top bar. Tufte small multiples — throughput + cumulative side-by-side. ISA-101/HMI hierarchy — alarm → process variable → trend → diagnostic. Industrial color: green/amber/red for state only; charts grey so color signals action.

SYSTEM HEALTH UX: Separate daemon/process state (live /health, display "up") from workload/backlog (telemetry, e.g. "up · 20"). Overall WARN when backlog exists even if daemons up. Single-line cells with detail in tooltips to avoid visual noise.

VISUAL THEME: Dark industrial console (#2a2a2a base), high-contrast text, green #56d364 / amber #f0c14a / red #ff7b72 for status; shared theme.css for dashboard + logs.

PLANNED LAYOUT (approved direction, not yet fully implemented): Two-column body — main ~68% (slim alert, backlog trend chart, throughput|cumulative grid, growth, raw samples table always visible) + sticky sidebar ~32% (backlog number+spark, bottleneck REM/NREM bar, pipeline 2×2, system health, schema breakdown collapsed). Remove or slim KPI strip to ≤4 chips or merge into sidebar. Widen to min(1600px, 100%-2rem). Responsive stack under 1100px.

IMPLEMENTATION BUGS FOUND: Duplicate const bn in render() broke all dashboard JS; rename backlog variable. Avoid declaring duplicate const in same function scope.

FILES: shared-memory-monitor/static/dashboard.html, static/logs.html, static/theme.css, src/sm_telemetry_monitor/system_health.py.

FRAMEWORK TELEMETRY GAPS for Shared Memory Monitor (measured 2026-07-16 after monitor v0.5.4 aligned to gateway 0.7.0 / API v3). Monitor remains pure observer (bridge.py + logs_reader only; monitor:read token). SURFACED on 0.7.0: health.config, spine, compliance, latency, entity_graph (incl. largest_alias_component), consolidation rollup, pool_busy. NOT surfaced — for framework agent review:

1) RELATION CALIBRATION STATE — lives only on write-role POST /memory/relations/review (+ /label). monitor:read gets HTTP 403. No top-level block on GET /memory/telemetry. Families entity_relation + evidential stay invisible to synthesis until ~20 operator labels, but the monitor cannot show calibrated/uncalibrated / label counts / queue depth. ASK: add telemetry.calibration (or spine.relation_adjudications) readable by monitor:read — status per family, labels_n, threshold, edges awaiting review. Do NOT put label mutations on the monitor.

2) CONSOLIDATION_RUNS.EXTRA not rolled up — daemon writes edges_awaiting_calibration, machine_edges_consumed, calibration snapshot into consolidation_runs.extra, but coordinator._compute_consolidation_health only exposes last_deferred_reason (extra->>'reason'). ASK: roll those counts into telemetry.consolidation.{insight,fact_consolidation} so the consolidation drawer can show machine-edge gate pressure without DB access.

3) NEO4J RETROSPECTIVE CENSUS — telemetry.neo4j still facts_total / decisions_* only. After retro-as-record (API v2 / 0.6.5) retrospectives are first-class records (live breakdown retrospective≈136) but no retrospectives_total / rem_pending. Spine.facts remains the non-decision bucket (honestly labeled in monitor UI). ASK: optional neo4j.retrospectives_* or spine split if census should be type-clean.

Principle held: if the monitor needs a metric, extend GET /health or GET /memory/telemetry — never invent a monitor-side DB path or borrow write tokens.
